gaps.sentence: The minister was ___ (CRITIC) for her handling of the flooding crisis.
gaps.explanation: 'Be criticised for' = be attacked verbally; the verb form is needed in the passive.

gaps.sentence: The factory will ___ (EMPLOY) fifty more workers next year.
gaps.explanation: The bare verb follows 'will': will employ.

gaps.sentence: Much to everyone’s ___ (APPOINT), the open-air concert was cancelled.
gaps.explanation: 'To somebody’s disappointment' — the feeling noun follows the possessive.

gaps.sentence: The council rejected plans for a new ___ (DEVELOP).
gaps.explanation: 'A development' = a building project; 'developer' = the company.

gaps.sentence: He made a full ___ (RECOVER) after six months.
The team celebrated a quick ___ (SOLVE) to the crisis.
gaps.explanation: 'A solution to the crisis' — the noun.

gaps.sentence: His ___ (REFUSE) to cooperate stalled the negotiations.
